Same as above, played the first few DotP first. Then I Vorthos'd out and didn't play much. Online DotP is cool.

I highly recommend two things: reading out loud (MULTIPLE times, S L O W L Y) and reading how cards interact and work (example here). You might run into a similar situation with a different card and have some insight as to how to act next. 

The Stack - Main thing I've found is that I have trouble understanding the little ins-and-outs of the stack, then randomly combat eludes me. Mastering the stack is like, jedi status. 

Random card on Gatherer - I think it's really fun to press random card. I would read the comments and see what combos people posted. I'd try to read the card mechanics and see if I could understand the combo before reading comments, but most of the time I didn't.  

Player types - It might feel like horoscopes, but identifying how you enjoy MtG can further the experience.

I agree with everything the others have said, and would like to add a great way to get into the game: the Deckbuilder's Toolkit. It's only 20$ for a total of 250 cards, and comes with a few guides on building decks and playing. It's what I used to get started, and it's great for newbies imo.

For tips on getting started playing in general I can't recommend enough the Intro Packs. They come with a fully-playable well built 60 card deck that may not be amazing but is solid and perfectly playable against anyone else. Plus 3 boosters so you get to experience cracking open a new pack and seeing what you found.

They also ship with a helpful rules "Quick Start Guide" card that folds up to a card size (so you can keep it with your deck) and has the turn order listed out which is typically the most confusing thing for new players to understand.

If you're looking for a good 2-player game for you and your roommate/SO/buddy to play the Duel Decks are good packages, too, since they ship with two decks specifically built and balanced to make for good match ups against each other.
